question: If strong AI models can run on our own phones, who should decide what they are allowed to do?
reflection: When capable tools run close to the people who use them, more communities can build for their own needs while keeping their data at home.

sources.subject: Thinking Machines Inkling, OpenAI GPT-Red Security, PrismML 27B

one_line: Open models are catching up fast: a new multimodal open model, a phone-sized 27B model and AI that attacks other AI to make it safer all arrived on the same day.

top_stories.title: Thinking Machines releases its first open model
top_stories.what: Thinking Machines Lab published Inkling, an open-weight model that handles text, images and audio in one design, with a very long context and a setting to raise or lower how much it reasons.
top_stories.why: A free, modifiable model that understands speech and documents could be run privately for interview and survey analysis.

top_stories.title: OpenAI trains an AI to attack its own models
top_stories.what: OpenAI says its GPT-Red system learns by playing attacker against defender models and found weaknesses in far more test cases than human testers did.
top_stories.why: Automated attack testing is becoming a normal part of deploying agents, which matters for any client putting AI near real transactions.

top_stories.title: A 27B model that fits on a phone
top_stories.what: PrismML released Bonsai 27B in very compressed versions, one small enough for a phone, and says it keeps most of the full model's quality.
top_stories.why: Capable offline AI makes private field data collection and analysis more realistic where connectivity or data rules are tight.

top_stories.title: A large reasoner trained without human labels
top_stories.what: Ant Group's Ling team reports a one-trillion-parameter reasoning model trained with no human-annotated examples.
top_stories.why: If this holds, the cost of building strong models in other languages and domains could fall.

saudi_lens.text: Open models that can run on local servers or phones fit Saudi rules on keeping sensitive data inside the Kingdom, and give local teams something they can adapt to Arabic.

idea.title: Offline interview assistant
idea.pitch: Test a phone-sized open model that summarises recorded field interviews without sending any audio to the cloud.
idea.first_step: Run a compressed open model on a test laptop and time how long it takes to summarise a ten-minute sample recording.

idea_kids.title: Red team and blue team
idea_kids.pitch: A table game where one team writes tricky instructions to fool a 'robot' card player and the other team writes rules to stop the tricks.
idea_kids.first_step: Write ten simple robot rules and ten trick cards, then play one round with family.

watchlist.name: Thinking Machines Lab
watchlist.note: First open model and a fine-tuning service; watch adoption by enterprises.

watchlist.name: PrismML
watchlist.note: Pushing large models onto phones through extreme compression.

tool.name: Bonsai 27B
tool.use: An open model small enough to test offline on a laptop or phone.

verify: GPT-Red reportedly succeeded in 84% of attack scenarios against 13% for human testers.
Bonsai 27B reportedly keeps 90% of full quality at under 4 GB.

terms.definition: An AI model whose trained settings are published so anyone can download, run and change it.
Deliberately attacking a system to find its weak points before real attackers do.
Storing a model's numbers with less precision so it needs much less memory, usually with a small loss in quality.
Hiding instructions inside content an AI reads so that it does something its user did not intend.

concepts.summary: Open models with text, audio and image skills narrow the gap with closed ones.
Large models compressed enough to run on a phone without the cloud.
AI attackers trained to find weaknesses in other AI before release.
